subject.title: sandbox: keep workspaceAccess none workspaces writable

question: Should OpenClaw restore writable isolated `/workspace` semantics for `workspaceAccess: "none"` across Docker and filesystem bridges now, and what live sandbox proof should be required before landing?
rationale: The product direction is strongly signaled by maintainer discussion, but the implementation changes sandbox write authorization and CODEOWNERS routes the affected paths to secops review.

options.title: Restore Isolated Writable None
options.body: Make only the sandbox-owned workspace writable for `none`, keep the real agent workspace hidden, and require backend parity tests plus live sandbox proof before merge.

options.title: Keep None Fail-Closed
options.body: Leave `none` read-only and update docs/tool exposure to match, accepting that this preserves the reported regression and contradicts the latest maintainer comment.

options.title: Split Core And Bind Policies
options.body: Fix isolated `/workspace` writability here and keep explicit host `:rw` bind authorization on https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/59718.

recommendation.title: Restore Isolated Writable None
recommendation.body: Make only the sandbox-owned workspace writable for `none`, keep the real agent workspace hidden, and require backend parity tests plus live sandbox proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: He is tied to the sandbox mount helper history and already made the clearest maintainer statement that this issue is the canonical writable-`none` fix path.
